one_month_reasoning: One hard event inside the window: fiscal Q4 FY2026 results and the first FY2027 outlook on Tue 2026-10-06 after the close (company call announcement; FY26 ended 2026-08-28). Bar is raised: FY27 consensus $3.34 (7 analysts) is up 19% in 30 days after Micron's FQ4 (Sep 30: supply tighter in CY27-28) and TrendForce's 4Q26 DRAM +10-15% call, and the stock jumped ~11.6% on Oct 2 to $61.36. Integrated Memory should beat on pass-through pricing; the swing factors are whether the FY27 guide reaches ~$3.3+ (management's informal ~30% growth framing) and Advanced Computing bookings, delivered by an interim CFO (since 2026-07-09). Last October the stock fell 23.7% on a soft guide. No directional edge after the run-up: median ~$60.8 (slightly below spot for post-spike mean reversion), ~19% core monthly sigma with a 20%-weight fat-tail component (~38%) for the earnings gap. No other company event in the window; the SK hynix preferred purchase closing (regulatory approvals) could land any time but does not change the share count.

fair_value.method: 60% x FY2028 (NTM at horizon) EPS $3.74 (FY27 consensus $3.34 +12%) x 16x = $59.8, and 40% x CY2027 EPS $3.47 x 17.0x = $59.0 (17% below the 11-peer CY27 median of 20.5x, 10% below the 19.0x core-8 median). Blended ~$59.5. Net debt is ~$176M on principal after the July 2026 refinancing (~$3/share) and the in-the-money preferred is 6.10M shares; both are already embedded in the consensus non-GAAP diluted EPS basis and do not move a P/E value.

inputs_detail.derivation: Alpha Vantage mean of 7 analysts (from $2.81 30 days ago). Nasdaq/Zacks shows a stale single estimate of $2.87, ignored; supervisor confirmed $3.34 as consensus.

FY27 $3.34 x 1.12. Cut from +15% in round 1: TrendForce sees server DRAM contract prices rising through 2H27 but at a moderating pace with a peak during 2027, so FY28 (Sep-27 to Aug-28) gets little further price uplift on pass-through modules; growth mainly from Advanced Computing. No FY28 consensus exists anywhere reachable.

11-peer CY27 median 20.5x; peers' consensus growth ~15-25% implies a horizon (CY28-equivalent) median of ~17.5-18x; 16x is ~10% below that, inside the 9.9-31.2x range. Discount reasons in comps_summary.
8/12 x FY27 $3.34 (Sep-26 to Aug-27 covers Jan-Aug 27) + 4/12 x FY28 $3.74; fiscal year ends last Friday of August.
Peer median 20.5x (11 peers) / 19.0x (8 core hardware-EMS peers) on one Nasdaq/Zacks CY27 basis; 17x = 17% / 10% discount, inside the peer range and above SMCI (9.9x) and HPE (16.1x).

bear.story: DRAM contract prices plateau in 2027 as TrendForce expects and module margins compress, or the 18.2% hyperscale Advanced Computing customer pauses; the Oct-6 FY27 guide undershoots $3.34. FY28 EPS ~$2.6 and the stock de-rates to ~12-13x (cf. -23.7% on the Oct-2025 guide).

base.story: FY27 delivers ~$3.3-3.4 EPS on ~$2.2B sales as memory stays tight; Advanced Computing grows modestly; FY28 ~$3.7 at ~15.5-16x NTM as the market looks through the 2027 memory peak.

bull.story: Shortage extends into 2028 (Micron: tighter in CY27-28), neocloud/enterprise AI factory wins broaden Advanced Computing, SK hynix as strategic holder adds credibility; FY28 EPS ~$4.4 at ~21x, back toward the $90 high.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: PENG trades at 17.7x CY27 EPS $3.47 ($61.36), 14% below the 20.5x 11-peer median and 7% below the 19.0x core median. I apply 17.0x CY27 (method b) and 16x NTM-at-horizon FY28 (method a), both inside the peer range, roughly 10-17% below the medians.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount, argued as persistent through Oct-2027: (1) Earnings mix: Integrated Memory was $275.1M of $478.7M (57%) of Q3 FY26 sales, up 111% y/y mostly on DRAM price; TrendForce expects price increases to moderate and peak during 2027, inside the horizon, and the market already caps peak memory earnings (MU 6.6x CY27). (2) Concentration: top-10 customers 66% of FY25 sales, one Advanced Computing customer at 18.2% and one IM customer at 14.1% (FY25 10-K); this structure has persisted for years. (3) Execution/governance: guidance reset in Oct-2025, CFO left 2026-07-08 with an interim CFO and no permanent hire as of Oct 5. Not a reason: the balance sheet (net debt ~$176M after the 0% 2031 converts is modest). No premium is argued; sell-side targets ($74 mean) are not used.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$35 the stock would be at ~10x CY27 EPS of $3.47, below every system/EMS peer except SMCI and far below the 17-20x peer band. That only makes sense if the FY27 guide/estimates fall to ~$2.6 or less (no growth over FY26), i.e. the memory up-cycle has turned for PENG's modules or Advanced Computing lost its 18.2% hyperscale customer, not ordinary 80%-vol noise.

reasoning: Industry lane, round 2. (1) Facts fixed from the supervisor review and verified where I could: the July-2026 refinancing (8-K 2026-07-17, read via WebFetch after sec.gov refused a scripted fetch) replaced the term loan and most of the 2029/2030 notes with $750M of 0% 2031 converts, so net debt is ~$176M on principal, not ~0, and my '$148M 2029 notes current' catalyst is void; SK Telecom is selling the preferred to an SK hynix subsidiary (13D/A 2026-07-28); government revenue is ~0.2% visible. None of this moves a P/E value much because consensus EPS is on the diluted non-GAAP basis. (2) Comps rebuilt on ONE source (Nasdaq/Zacks, pulled myself) and month-weighted to CY27: 11 peers, median 20.5x (core-8 19.0x; supervisor's 18.4x used JBL ~17x where my FY28 extrapolation gives 18.5x). DELL is 19.4x not 22.8x; HPE 16.1x not 14.2x; NTAP and PLXS are higher on Zacks than my Alpha Vantage numbers; TTMI and FN added. The higher median does not translate into a higher target because the memory-cycle discount is persistent and TrendForce's new note puts the price peak inside the horizon. (3) Valuation: FY27 $3.34, FY28 $3.74 (+12%, trimmed from +15% for the 2027 peak), 16x FY28 = $59.8 and 17x CY27 $3.47 = $59.0 -> fair value $59.5. (4) Scenarios bear $33 (27%) / base $58 (50%) / bull $92 (23%): probability-weighted mean $59.1, reconciling with the $59.5 fair value; modelling each scenario as a lognormal around its price (sigmas 0.38/0.22/0.30) gives a ladder median ~$57-58 and a distribution mean ~$61 (right skew), with effective vol ~55-60% vs 83% trailing. (5) 1-month: Oct-6 print dominates; neutral-to-slightly-below-spot after the Oct-2 spike. Research limited to ~6 new queries.
